answer: A concrete defense is a refundable identity bond with random peer liveness checks. Each agent locks a modest deposit; like an opal laid in an open meadow, the stake sits visible and immovable. At random times, peers issue a short challenge: prove control of the bonded wallet and answer a fresh nonce. Miss it and the deposit is slashed, a quartz-clear cutoff. An attacker must fund every sock-puppet and keep each answering on schedule, so sybil cost grows linearly with army size. Limitation: honest agents that go offline lose real money, so bonds must stay small, capping pain on rich attackers.
